(a) concavity is the most general property of the free energy and other thermodynamical functions of a mixture of nuclei, and (b) the concavity of the average energy is the only condition to obtain a sequence of upper and lower bounds to the binding energy of a nucleus.

the concavity of the grand potential and other thermodynamical functions for a mixture of nuclear matter and its possible use in the prediction of binding and excitation energies.
